page: Microsoft Azure E64-32ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained core configuration. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU, and integrates 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The AMD processor supports advanced vector instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-threaded throughput and memory capabilities. The instance achieved a top-tier rating in single-core stress-ng tests (3789.09) and single-threaded gzip compression (40.71 GB/sec). Multi-core processing and PassMark CPU evaluations placed in the upper quartiles, scoring 56492.78 and 58651.77 respectively. Uncached memory read bandwidth measured 102.21 GB/sec, while write operations sustained 67.4 GB/sec. In-memory data throughput reached 53.36 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks, while lightweight LLM inference achieved 435.32 tokens per second for small-scale generation.

The constrained-core architecture offers distinct licensing cost efficiency by provisioning the full 512.0 GB memory footprint and 3780 GB local NVMe storage of a standard 64-vCPU chassis while utilizing only 32 vCPUs. This configuration significantly reduces per-core software licensing costs for memory-bound applications. However, compute throughput scales only to 32 vCPUs, as reflected in average multi-core results and reduced performance during large-model LLM generation.

Azure E64-32ads_v7 is tailored for enterprise memory-intensive workloads that require substantial RAM and high IOPS without requiring excessive compute parallelism. Well-matched use cases include large relational databases (such as Microsoft SQL Server or Oracle), in-memory caching systems, transactional datastores, and batch analytics engines.
